certifications.name: SEC1 (Cyber Security 101)
certifications.desc: A foundational, fully hands-on certification rather than a multiple-choice one — unusual at this level, where almost everything else tests recall. A reasonable first certificate for someone with no background at all.

certifications.name: CompTIA Security+
certifications.desc: A broad, vendor-neutral security credential covering concepts, operations, and governance. It includes knowledge and performance-based questions; hands-on practice still matters.
certifications.readiness: Build broad security knowledge and use the current exam objectives; a single KashSec path covers only part of them.

certifications.name: eJPT (Junior Penetration Tester)
certifications.desc: Hands-on, affordable, practical intro to pentesting — a good first hands-on cert before OSCP.
certifications.readiness: Practice network enumeration, web testing, and reporting in authorized labs; review the provider preparation.

certifications.name: ISC2 Certified in Cybersecurity (CC)
certifications.desc: A broad foundations credential for people starting a cybersecurity career.
certifications.readiness: No work experience is required. Study the full current outline beyond these course foundations.

certifications.name: PCEP — Certified Entry-Level Python Programmer
certifications.desc: An optional programming credential focused on Python fundamentals.
certifications.format: Knowledge exam; see current provider guide
certifications.readiness: Write and debug your own small programs first. This is a programming credential, not a security specialization.

certifications.name: SAL1 (Security Analyst Level 1)
certifications.desc: A SOC analyst certification scored mostly on simulated shift work: a short multiple-choice section for the theory, then two separate SOC simulations where you triage and close real alerts. The simulations carry the large majority of the marks, which is the right way round. Valid three years.

certifications.name: CompTIA CySA+
certifications.desc: Blue-team focused: SOC analysis, threat detection, incident response fundamentals.

certifications.name: CEH (Certified Ethical Hacker)
certifications.desc: Broad, theory-heavy overview of hacking tools and methodology — widely known, though many employers weight practical certs higher.

certifications.name: Cisco Certified Network Associate (CCNA)
certifications.desc: A networking credential covering network operation, access, IP services, security fundamentals, and automation.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current Cisco guide
certifications.readiness: Add routing, switching, device configuration, and troubleshooting practice beyond these paths.

certifications.name: Certificate of Cloud Security Knowledge (CCSK)
certifications.desc: A vendor-neutral certificate of cloud security knowledge.
certifications.format: Online knowledge exam; see current CSA guide
certifications.readiness: Use the full CSA study material. This knowledge certificate is separate from professional experience-based credentials.

certifications.name: PT1 (Junior Penetration Tester)
certifications.desc: Sat inside a pentest simulator against web, network and Active Directory targets, and finished by writing a professional report. The report is not an afterthought — being unable to write up a finding is what actually stops people getting hired.

certifications.name: CompTIA PenTest+
certifications.desc: A middle ground between Security+ and OSCP — pentesting methodology, tools, and reporting, mixed multiple-choice and performance-based questions.

certifications.name: PNPT (Practical Network Penetration Tester)
certifications.desc: A full practical pentest engagement against a live network, including a real written report — closely mirrors real consulting work.
certifications.readiness: Build practical network and Active Directory assessment skills, including a report and debrief.

certifications.name: OSCP (Offensive Security Certified Professional)
certifications.desc: The industry-recognized "can you actually hack things" cert — a 24-hour hands-on exam. Widely respected, genuinely hard.
certifications.readiness: Advanced practical preparation is needed beyond this course. Check the current OSCP/OSCP+ exam and designation policies.

certifications.name: Linux Foundation Certified System Administrator (LFCS)
certifications.desc: A practical system-administration credential for a Linux operations role.
certifications.readiness: Practice on real Linux systems and follow the current administration objectives, not only security commands.

certifications.name: Microsoft Identity and Access Administrator Associate (SC-300)
certifications.desc: An identity-administration option focused on Microsoft Entra ID.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current Microsoft guide
certifications.readiness: Requires additional hands-on Microsoft Entra administration and study of the current SC-300 objectives.

certifications.name: Burp Suite Certified Practitioner (BSCP)
certifications.desc: A practical credential focused on web application testing with Burp Suite.
certifications.readiness: Work through the provider preparation steps and labs. An active Burp Suite Professional subscription is needed for the exam.

certifications.name: GIAC AI certifications (GOAA, GAIPS, GASAE)
certifications.desc: Separate GIAC credentials covering offensive AI, AI security, and security automation. Compare the individual outlines and exam formats; this group is not one certification.
certifications.format: Separate exams; check each current GIAC guide

certifications.name: GIAC Cloud Security Automation (GCSA)
certifications.desc: A specialist option for cloud security automation and DevSecOps practices.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current GIAC guide
certifications.readiness: Build practical cloud, pipeline, and automation skills. Compare the complete outline and funding options before booking.

certifications.name: GIAC Mobile Device Security Analyst (GMOB)
certifications.desc: A specialist mobile-device security credential; compare its scope with your intended role.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current GIAC guide
certifications.readiness: Add platform, device, and mobile assessment practice. This path is a starting point rather than a full exam course.

certifications.name: Global Industrial Cyber Security Professional (GICSP)
certifications.desc: A specialist credential linking industrial operations and cybersecurity.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current GIAC guide
certifications.readiness: Study the complete industrial security outline and operational context. Course simulations do not establish competence to test live OT.

certifications.name: OSAI / OSAI+ (Advanced AI Red Teaming, AI-300)
certifications.desc: OffSec's AI red teaming certification, launched March 2026 — the first from the people behind OSCP. A 24-hour practical engagement against AI-integrated systems, in the same shape as the OSCP exam but aimed at model and pipeline attacks. OSAI does not expire; the OSAI+ designation lapses after three years.

certifications.name: HTB COAE (Certified Offensive AI Expert)
certifications.desc: Built with Google and aligned to their Secure AI Framework. A seven-day practical engagement against AI-driven infrastructure, finished with a commercial-grade report, covering adversarial ML, model privacy attacks, LLM output abuse and supply-chain risk. Requires completing the AI Red Teamer path first — the certification and that path are different things, and are often confused.
certifications.readiness: Advanced goal: follow the provider prerequisites and AI Red Teamer preparation; needs substantial Python, ML, and web-testing practice.

certifications.name: AWS Certified Security — Specialty
certifications.desc: A specialist option for securing AWS workloads and operations.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current AWS guide
certifications.readiness: A later goal for people with substantial practical AWS security experience; check the provider candidate profile.

certifications.name: Certified Secure Software Lifecycle Professional (CSSLP)
certifications.desc: A secure software lifecycle credential covering requirements, design, implementation, testing, operations, and supply chain.
certifications.readiness: Certification requires four years of relevant experience, subject to eligible waivers, and endorsement. The Associate of ISC2 route is available after passing without the required experience; check the current rules.

certifications.name: Certified Kubernetes Security Specialist (CKS)
certifications.desc: A practical credential for securing Kubernetes clusters and workloads.
certifications.readiness: You must already have passed the CKA exam; it does not need to remain active. Add substantial cluster administration and hardening practice.

certifications.name: GIAC Reverse Engineering Malware (GREM)
certifications.desc: A specialist credential focused on reverse engineering and malware analysis.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current GIAC guide
certifications.readiness: Build substantial disassembly and isolated analysis experience before considering this specialist exam.

certifications.name: Certified Information Systems Auditor (CISA)
certifications.desc: An audit-focused credential for assessing information systems controls and assurance.
certifications.format: Proctored exam; see current ISACA guide
certifications.readiness: Certification normally requires five years of qualifying experience, subject to allowed substitutions. The exam can be taken earlier; passing alone does not confer CISA.
